title: PithTrain: A Compact and Agent-Native MoE Training System
claim: A system built on agent-native design principles gives both training efficiency and agent-task efficiency, assessed by a benchmark of agent tasks.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, dashed zoom lines linking agent loop to system details
description: A three-part figure read left to right. On the left, an Agent (robot icon) sits in a rounded loop with PithTrain, the agent-native training system. Arrows labeled 'actions' and 'feedback' connect them, and an optional 'Agent Skills' box sits on the feedback path. Dashed zoom lines open the middle panel. It has an orange box of four design principles: compact codebase, no implicit indirection, Python-native, and task-specific agent skills. Below that is a small MoE training diagram, from input tokens through Attn and MoE layers to loss and backward pass. Green boxes at the bottom label 'Dual Efficiency': training efficiency and agent-task efficiency. The right panel is the ATE-Bench box. It shows a task, framework, agent and metrics setup, plus color-coded task categories: Q&A, Operate & Profile, and New Feature. The palette is soft pastels, with gray, orange, green, blue and purple.
caption: PithTrain overview. An agent issues actions and consumes feedback (left); built on four agent-native design principles, PithTrain delivers dual efficiency (middle); ATE-Bench evaluates agent-task efficiency across frameworks (right).
abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) has become the dominant architecture for frontier language models. To meet this demand, production frameworks have built optimized MoE training stacks over years of engineering effort. Yet evolving these stacks for new architectures and system optimizations remains expensive. With the rise of AI coding agents, they could automate parts of training-framework development and accelerate this evolution. But applying them to these existing frameworks carries hidden costs, invisible to today's throughput-only evaluations. We name this missing dimension agent-task efficiency (ATE): the cost of using coding agents to understand, operate, and extend a framework. Grounded in four agent-native design principles, we build PithTrain, a compact, agent-native MoE training framework supporting pretraining, supervised fine-tuning, and reinforcement learning. We further introduce ATE-Bench, covering real-world training-framework tasks. Our evaluation shows PithTrain achieves throughput competitive with production frameworks and higher agent-task efficiency on ATE-Bench. On new-feature tasks, PithTrain uses up to 62% fewer Agent Turns than Megatron-LM, and up to 44% and 64% less Active GPU Time than Megatron-LM and TorchTitan, respectively.
